title: Feedback loops may be conducive to pathway memory but are not the only route

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Feedback loops may be conducive to pathway memory but are not the only route

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Self-sustaining feedback loops with hysteresis, such as the positive-feedback dual phosphorylation–dephosphorylation cycle of MAPK, may be conducive to memory in biochemical networks, but feedback loop architecture may be only one of many ways to support such memories.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.1. Biological Networks May Possess Multiple Types of Memory

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Overall, we suggest that feedback loop network architecture may be conducive to memories but may be only one way of many to support them.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Biswas S, Clawson W, Levin M, “Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions”, International journal of molecular sciences (2022), doi:10.3390/ijms24010285; section “2. Results › 2.1. Biological Networks May Possess Multiple Types of Memory”. Scope: Biochemical reaction networks, e.g. MAPK phosphorylation cycles

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-grn-learning-07: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.62

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public models permit a comparative association test, but the modal wording and incomplete sampling prevent a decisive general conclusion. Causal attribution to architecture is also confounded by kinetics.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Annotate feedback and hysteresis in a broad model collection and test whether these features predict memory after controlling for size and dynamics. Memory in rigorously feedback-free networks would support the existence of other routes.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The terms 'conducive' and 'many ways' lack prespecified effect sizes.

Feedback can be represented implicitly in kinetic equations.

fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.62
data adequacy: 0.52

data existence: 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Loop structure and memory labels are both recoverable from public models and code. The wording is permissive, and the MAPK example does not isolate feedback from other dynamics. The analysis can check co-occurrence, not that loops are a cause or that they are dispensable in general.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Classify feedback loops and hysteresis in the BioModels SBML graphs, then compare memory prevalence in models with and without those loops. Memory enriched in loop-containing models, plus at least some memory in models that lack them, would support the hedged claim; memory absent outside loops, or no enrichment, would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Feedback is common in published pathway models, so co-occurrence is a weak causal test.

'May be conducive' and 'one way of many' are hard to refute with a binary loop count.

analysis feasibility: 0.55
